description.narrative:
Swedac and SIS will support Ukraine to:
- Maintain the most important aspects of QI (Quality Infrastructure) during the war to sustain trade and vital public services. As a result, it will increase export to the EU during the war.
- Strengthening the Ukrainian QI after the war to promote trade and support a green reconstruction. As a result, the short-term increase of export to EU and investment in export-oriented facilities. These investments will lead to increasing in export in the long term.
- Support the institutions within the QI in Ukraine in their adaptation to, and integration with, the EU. Integrated institutions will increase trust from local investors, as well as from foreign investors. It will lead to rising in long-term investment in export-oriented facilities.

Ukraina är i en EU-närmandeprocess. Kvalitetsinfrastruktur (KI) är en betydelsefull faktor för den ekonomiska integreringen. Swedac och SIS kommer att stödja Ukraina med att upprätthålla de viktigaste aspekterna av KI medan kriget pågår för att upprätthålla handel och viktiga offentliga tjänster; att stärka den ukrainska KI efter kriget för att främja handel och stödja en grön återuppbyggnad; att stödja institutionerna inom KI i Ukraina i deras anpassning till och integration med EU.

Ukraine is in the process of EU integration. Quality infrastructure (QI) is a significant factor in economic integration. Swedac and SIS will support Ukraine to maintain the most important aspects of QI while the war continues to sustain trade and vital public services; strengthening the Ukrainian QI after the war to promote trade and support a green reconstruction; support the institutions within the QI in Ukraine in their adaptation to, and integration with, the EU.

Since the project is in an early stage of implementation there are still few results to report from 2024. Below is a summary of the main achievements:
Accreditation
The study visit on accreditation in October 2024 played a role in strengthening cooperation between the Ministry of Economy of Ukraine (MEU) and the National Accreditation Agency of Ukraine (NAAU). Discussions facilitated better coordination and understanding of accreditations role in notified body oversight. One of the main results was that the information shared was useful when MEU initiate a of regulatory reform to update accreditation regulations in the metrology sector, following EU expert recommendations.
Legal Metrology
A study visit in October 2024 provided Ukrainian stakeholders with a deeper understanding of EU legal metrology practices. Discussions emphasized financial models, oversight mechanisms, and risk-based approaches to supervision. The visit also strengthened dialogue between regulatory agencies, paving the way for necessary structural reforms in 2025 to align Ukraines system with EU requirements.
Market Surveillance
Ukraine continued to develop its market surveillance system in line with EU expectations. A key milestone was the drafting of a new Market Surveillance Law, addressing EU recommendations from the ACAA screening process. The study visit in October 2024 facilitated knowledge-sharing on EU best practices and risk-based enforcement. Cooperation between government agencies improved, and discussions on establishing a centralized coordination office for market surveillance advanced.
Notifying Authority
A component of the project was the support provided to Ukraine in establishing a functional notifying authority in accordance with EU requirements. The study visit in October 2024 provided Ukrainian stakeholders with a deeper understanding of the governance, responsibilities, and operational requirements of notifying authorities.
Standardization
The Swedish Institute for Standards (SIS) played a role in supporting Ukraines EU integration efforts by organizing a webinar on EU standardization principles, attended by over 50 stakeholders. Additionally, SIS supported the translation and distribution of The Blue Guide on EU product rules 2022, along with 12 key ISO and CEN guides, equipping Ukrainian institutions with essential knowledge for harmonizing their standardization framework with EU norms.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
